union.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` uses a super-linear (quadratic) trailing-whitespace regex — ReDoS on attacker-supplied note content
union.evidence:
The new plugin re-implements markdown-it's trim as `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 20) applied via `str.replace` in `asciiTrim` (line 22), and calls it on `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` in the replaced `lheading` rule. `[class]+$` with a global replace is the classic quadratic trim pattern: for every index inside a whitespace run the engine greedily consumes the run, fails `$` because non-whitespace follows, and backtracks one char at a time — O(n^2) in the length of the run.

Vector: a collaborator (notes live in a shared Yorkie doc, so content is not self-authored only) writes a setext heading whose paragraph body ends in a long run of spaces followed by a non-whitespace char, e.g. `"a" + " ".repeat(1_000_000) + "\nb\n==="`. `lheadingRule` sets `level=1`, computes `content`, and `asciiTrim` then does ~1e12 backtracking steps, hanging the main thread of every viewer's preview pane (browser tab freeze / unresponsive editor). Native `String.prototype.trim()` (or a single-pass index scan) is linear and would avoid this entirely; the code chose the regex only to avoid importing a private markdown-it helper.

How far I got: I could not confirm upstream markdown-it 14.x uses an identically-shaped regex (if it does, this is pre-existing rather than newly introduced), nor whether any length cap exists on `preview.render()` input — the `packages/` tree is not present in the materialized working copy I was given (only `agent/`, `hooks/`, verify-*.mjs), so I could not grep the real call sites or node_modules. Hence medium confidence on novelty, high confidence on the regex's complexity class.

union.summary: Forked copy of upstream `lheading` plus reliance on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry: future upstream hardening/DoS fixes are silently not inherited, and an internals rename throws at module load
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` swaps in a hand-copied duplicate of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`. Any security or DoS hardening markdown-it later lands in that rule (it is a rule that loops over lines and calls every paragraph terminator, i.e. a plausible place for pathological-input fixes) will be shipped by `npm update` but never take effect in the notes preview — a silent divergence with no test or lint that notices. Separately, `getRuleFn` reads the undocumented private `ruler.__rules__` array (line ~207) and `throw`s `markdown-it block rule not found: list` when the shape changes; because `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` runs at module evaluation time in `preview.ts`, that throw happens at import, taking the whole preview module (and anything importing it) down rather than degrading. Both are availability/maintainability hardening concerns rather than an exploitable flaw today.

union.summary: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode without delegating, so paragraph termination is decided by a guard that does not verify the stock `list` rule would actually accept the line
union.evidence: In `wrappedList` (lines 179-190) the branch `silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)` returns `true` immediately, asserting the paragraph ends here without asking the original `list` rule. `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` plus marker/whitespace shape, whereas upstream `list` applies extra rejections (e.g. the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4` deep-indent paragraph-continuation case, marker-style-change handling). If any input reaches this branch where the subsequent non-silent `list` call returns `false`, the line falls through to `paragraph`, which still consumes it — so I traced no non-terminating loop and no `state.line` non-advance (markdown-it's tokenizer only calls rules with `silent=false`, so this branch can never be the rule that fails to advance). Reporting as a low-confidence availability concern only: I could not construct a hang, and I could not run the parser because `packages/notes` is absent from the materialized tree.

union.summary: New hand-rolled `asciiTrim` replaces upstream's linear `String.prototype.trim()` with a quadratic-backtracking regex on attacker-controlled note text (ReDoS / main-thread freeze for every collaborator)
union.evidence: The vendored `lheading` copy ends with `asciiTrim(state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false))` (line 134-136). Upstream markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses `.trim()` there, which is O(n); this diff swaps in `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 19-20) used via `String.replace` with the `g` flag. The trailing alternative `[ws]+$` is retried at every offset inside a whitespace run: for a run of k whitespace characters not at end-of-string the engine does O(k) greedy-match-then-backtrack work per starting offset, i.e. O(k^2) total. Attack: a workspace member stores a note containing `A` + 200_000 spaces + `B\n===` (a setext heading whose content holds one long whitespace run — the only branch that reaches `asciiTrim`, since it runs on the heading-found path). `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:150` (`renderPreview = () => preview.render(currentDoc())`) re-renders synchronously on *every* document change, local **and remote** (see the comment at editor.ts:95-96), and `preview.ts:165` does `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(markdown)`. So the quadratic scan runs on the victim's main thread each time the malicious content syncs in, freezing the tab of anyone who opens or is joined to the note — and the victim cannot edit the doc to remove it because the tab is wedged. Not exponential, so severity is a persistent availability hit on a shared resource rather than instant kill; using `.trim()` (as upstream does) or a two-pass index scan removes it entirely.

union.summary: Vendored fork of markdown-it's `lheading` block rule plus private-`__rules__` reflection: upstream security/robustness fixes to the setext rule silently stop applying to the notes preview
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (line 175) permanently replaces the dependency's own rule with a copy of markdown-it 14.x internals pasted into the repo (lines 70-155), and `getRuleFn` (lines 207-214) reaches into the undocumented `ruler.__rules__` registry to fetch `list`. Consequence in my lane: the notes preview is the one place in the product that parses untrusted collaborator markdown (`preview.ts:120-127` documents the stored-XSS posture), and any future markdown-it patch to `lheading` — e.g. a DoS/quadratic-scan or heading-content-handling fix — will be shipped by `npm update` but never reach this forked copy, which no longer tracks upstream. `markdown-it: ^14.1.0` (packages/notes/package.json:63) is a caret range, so minor upgrades land silently while the fork stays frozen. Secondary: because `getRuleFn` `throw`s from a module-scope `md.use(...)`, an internals rename turns a rendering divergence into a hard import-time failure of the preview module (availability). Mitigation: derive from `md.block.ruler.getRules(...)`/wrap rather than re-implement, and pin the markdown-it version the copy was taken from.

union.summary: Deliberate CommonMark divergence means the same note bytes render differently in the Wafflebase preview than in any other renderer (content-spoofing surface if note markdown is ever rendered elsewhere)
union.evidence:
`wrappedList` lets an empty bullet interrupt a paragraph and the replaced `lheading` refuses a lone `-` underline, so `- 1\n -` renders as body text + empty nested item here while cmark-gfm/GitHub render `

1

`. Today `NotePreview` is the only consumer (grep for `md.render`/`new MarkdownIt` across `packages/` returns only `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165`), so nothing is exploitable now. Flagged only because render-divergence between a viewer a human approves content in and a second renderer of the same bytes is a classic spoofing primitive: if note markdown later feeds an export, email, or server-side render, attacker text could be shown as innocuous in-preview and as an authoritative heading downstream. Keeping the deviation confined to the preview instance (as done) is the right containment; a test asserting no other renderer picks up the plugin would lock it in.
